_note: Sorting by garbage category. Bins stay on map row y = 13 cm (markers 40-44, ~20 cm from the base, pitch 145-150). The category comes from the official 3-class model (Fish_bone->kitchen, Newspaper->recyclable, Syringe->hazardous; no 'other' class) when it is confident and agrees with the block colour; the colour -> category mapping is a fact of this block set (docs/atlas-200i-dk-a2/07) and decides when the model is silent or disagrees.
_bins_note: Physical acrylic bins (config/bins_acrylic_*.json, docs/atlas-200i-dk-a2/24). Used when run.py is given --bins: the block is let go over the bin opening instead of set down on a map code. slots_cm are drop points in the bin frame (x right, +Y to the flange), filled in order; 3 cm blocks in an 80 mm opening. +-1.2 cm chosen in simulation (2026-10-30, bins off by 8 mm / 4 deg, joints off by 1.5 deg: 8 of 8 in; +-1.8 cm: 2 of 4 hung on the rim). A bin counts as full after as many blocks as it has slots (data/runs/bins_state.json keeps the count; run.py --empty-bins resets it). Design values, not tried on the real arm.

bins._drop_offset_note: Per bin, [dx, dy] cm in the bin frame (x to the right looking from the arm, +y away from the arm), ADDED to the slot's drop point. 0 = the model as it is. 2026-11-06 real arm: bin 2 block came to rest toward the bin's edge, bin 3 block 'near the left edge' after a bounce, roughly 1-2 cm off. Fill in from measured landings (centre of the block against the bin centre, after subtracting the slot): if it lands 1.5 cm too far left, put +1.5 in dx.
